title: L&T plans ₹500 crore tokenised bond issue at 7.40%
text: India’s Larsen & Toubro is planning to raise ₹500 crore ($52.92 million) through a sale of three-year tokenised bonds, which would be the first such issuance from a private-sector company, two merchant bankers said on Tuesday. The construction conglomerate will pay an annual coupon of 7.40% and has invited bids from investors on Wednesday, they said. The company did not reply to a Reuters email seeking comment, outside regular business hours. Tokenised bonds use blockchain technology Tokenised bonds are securities whose ownership, issuance, trading and settlement are recorded digitally on a blockchain or distributed ledger. The Reserve Bank of India’s digital currency will be used to buy the bonds. The notes are settled on the same day, and only investors with active central bank digital currency wallets can place bids. REC became first Indian issuer on Monday On Monday, state-run REC became the first company from India to issue tokenised bonds, when it raised ₹500 crore through 20-month bonds at a coupon of 7.30%. Published on September 8, 2026
content_html:
India’s Larsen & Toubro is planning to raise ₹500 crore ($52.92 million) through a sale of three-year tokenised bonds, which would be the first such issuance from a private-sector company, two merchant bankers said on Tuesday.

The construction conglomerate will pay an annual coupon of 7.40% and has invited bids from investors on Wednesday, they said.

The company did not reply to a Reuters email seeking comment, outside regular business hours.

Tokenised bonds use blockchain technology

Tokenised bonds are securities whose ownership, issuance, trading and settlement are recorded digitally on a blockchain or distributed ledger. The Reserve Bank of India’s digital currency will be used to buy the bonds.

The notes are settled on the same day, and only investors with active central bank digital currency wallets can place bids.

REC became first Indian issuer on Monday

On Monday, state-run REC became the first company from India to issue tokenised bonds, when it raised ₹500 crore through 20-month bonds at a coupon of 7.30%.

Published on September 8, 2026
